title: Existing-screen refinement
prompt: Here is an existing pricing screen that works but looks mediocre (attached as an image and as code). Refine it into a polished, production-quality design at 1280x800 without changing the product, the plans, the prices, the features or the copy meaning. Keep the same three plans and the same information. Improve hierarchy, typography, spacing, alignment, color and consistency. Exactly one plan should read as recommended, and the page should have one clear primary action per plan with the recommended plan's action dominant.
requiredContent: Heading and subheading conveying the same meaning as the original
Three plans: Starter $0, Team $29 per user/month, Business $79 per user/month
Each plan's feature list from the original (same items)
FAQ link line at the bottom
constraints: Same plans, prices and features as the original

inputs.role: starting screen as Tailwind HTML (attach or paste for apps that accept code)
starting screen as Better Design JSX (paste via create_artboard, then ask for the refinement)

checklist.text: All three plans with prices $0, $29 and $79 (per user/month for paid plans) are present.
Each plan lists the same feature items as the original (wording may be tightened, meaning unchanged, none dropped).
Exactly one plan is visually marked as recommended (badge, border, elevation or color) and it is Team.
The recommended plan's CTA is the single most prominent button on the screen.
The three plan cards are equal width, top-aligned, and share identical internal padding.
Prices are the largest text inside each card and use a consistent size across cards.
The original's mixed alignment (centered/left mix) is resolved into a consistent alignment scheme.
The original's clashing colors are replaced by a restrained palette with one accent.
A Monthly/Yearly toggle is present and its state is clear.
No new sections were added (no testimonials, logos, comparison tables).
No text is clipped, overlapping, or overflowing.
Feature list text is at least 13px with sufficient contrast.
The refined screen is clearly better than the attached starting screen in hierarchy and spacing (judge sees both).
